cases.description: The key set records the key as retired on 2026-01-10; the payload CLAIMS issuedAt 2026-01-15. The state is KEY_RETIRED. No anomaly is flagged and nothing is concluded about when the signature was really made.

cases.name: key-state.retired.issuedAt-before-retiredAt
cases.description: The key set records the key as retired on 2026-02-01; the payload claims issuedAt 2026-01-15. Also KEY_RETIRED: identical to the other order, so no time inference is made either way. issuedAt is a signer claim, not trusted time.

cases.name: key-state.rotated-in-active
cases.description: The same content signed by the rotated-in key, which is active.

cases.name: key-state.revoked.revokedAt-after-issuedAt
cases.description: Revoked on 2026-01-20; claimed issuedAt is earlier. KEY_REVOKED regardless: after a compromise every signature under the key is suspect, whatever it says about time.

cases.name: key-state.revoked.revokedAt-before-issuedAt
cases.description: Revoked on 2026-01-01; claimed issuedAt is later. KEY_REVOKED, identically.

cases.name: key-state.purpose-mismatch
cases.description: The key is in the key set but declared for another purpose: KEY_PURPOSE_MISMATCH, distinct from a bad signature and from an unknown key. Integrity is unaffected.

cases.name: key-state.purpose-checked-before-revocation
cases.description: A revoked key with the wrong purpose reports KEY_PURPOSE_MISMATCH: the purpose is checked first. (Both are refused by every policy.)

cases.name: key-state.purpose-checked-before-retirement
cases.description: A retired key with the wrong purpose reports KEY_PURPOSE_MISMATCH, not KEY_RETIRED.

cases.name: key-state.unknown-key
cases.description: keyId absent from the key set.

cases.name: key-state.self-signed-attacker
cases.description: An internally consistent bundle signed by a key nobody published.

cases.name: key-state.issuer-mismatch
cases.description: Payload issuer is not the key set's issuer namespace.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.missing-purpose
cases.description: A key set entry with no purpose is not a usable key set: purpose must be explicit.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.keyId-mismatch
cases.description: A key set entry whose keyId is not the thumbprint of its own key.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.duplicate
cases.description: Two key set entries with the same keyId.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.private-material
cases.description: A key set entry carrying private key material.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.bad-status
cases.description: A key set entry with an unknown status.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.retired-without-date
cases.description: A retired entry without retiredAt.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.unknown-field
cases.description: A key set entry with an unknown field.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.non-canonical-coordinate
cases.description: A key set entry whose x is a non-canonical spelling: one key, one accepted spelling, one keyId.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.unknown-version
cases.description: An unknown keySetVersion fails closed.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.missing-sequence
cases.description: A key set without a sequence.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.sequence-zero
cases.description: sequence must be a positive integer.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.sequence-string
cases.description: sequence must be an integer, not a string.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.bad-generatedAt
cases.description: generatedAt must be a canonical timestamp (it is informational, but its form is strict).

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.unknown-top-level-field
cases.description: An unknown field on the key set itself.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.entry-purpose-empty
cases.description: A key set entry whose purpose is present but EMPTY: purpose must be explicit and non-empty. (Coverage vector added after the first v2 generation and before the v2 freeze.)

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.entry-notBefore-not-canonical
cases.description: A key set entry whose notBefore is not a canonical timestamp (2026-01-01 instead of 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z). (Coverage vector added after the first v2 generation and before the v2 freeze.)

cases.name: key-state.rollback.stale-key-set-for-the-correct-issuer
cases.description: The verifier retained sequence 5 FOR THIS ISSUER (agentverify-conformance, the issuer named in the bundle's own payload) and is offered a key set with sequence 3: KEY_SET_ROLLBACK_DETECTED. This is rollback DETECTION, and it works only because the verifier retained prior state for this issuer.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.sequence-equal-to-retained
cases.description: The same sequence as retained (7) is not behind it. The check says NOT_BEHIND_RETAINED: "not older than something already seen", which is not freshness.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.sequence-above-retained
cases.description: A higher sequence than retained is not behind it.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.no-retained-state
cases.description: No retained state at all: the result says NO_RETAINED_STATE. The sequence could not be checked, and that is NOT the same as "sequence confirmed": a verifier with no state learns nothing from the number.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.empty-retained-state
cases.description: An empty retained-state object is the same as none.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.low-sequence-with-no-state-is-accepted
cases.description: The same low-sequence (3) key set with no retained state is simply used, and reported as NO_RETAINED_STATE. The numbers alone protect nothing.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.other-issuers-state-is-ignored
cases.description: Retained state exists, but only for ANOTHER issuer (agentverify-other, sequence 99). It cannot affect this bundle: NO_RETAINED_STATE, and the low-sequence key set is not flagged.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.only-the-payload-issuer-counts
cases.description: Retained state for two issuers: the unrelated one (99) is ignored and the payload issuer's own (2) is used: not behind.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.issuer-a-state-cannot-affect-issuer-b
cases.description: A bundle issued under agentverify-other, with its own key set (sequence 2). Issuer A's retained sequence (99) cannot affect it.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.issuer-b-own-state-applies
cases.description: The same issuer-B bundle, with retained state for issuer B (5): now the stale key set is detected.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.key-set-for-another-issuer-consults-no-state
cases.description: A key set whose issuer is not the payload's issuer is not this issuer's key set: KEY_UNKNOWN, and NO retained state is consulted (no sequence check is reported).

cases.name: key-state.rollback.issuer-named-like-a-prototype-member
cases.description: An issuer literally named "constructor": retained state is read by OWN key only, so an empty state object has nothing for it (an inherited lookup would return a function).

cases.name: key-state.rollback.prototype-named-issuer-with-real-state
cases.description: The same issuer with real retained state (9): it is used, and the key set (sequence 4) is behind it.

cases.name: key-state.not-evaluated-when-integrity-fails
cases.description: Key state is never evaluated for a bundle whose integrity failed, even with a matching key set.

cases.name: policy.satisfied
cases.description: A policy that the bundle satisfies (default: only KEY_ACTIVE is accepted).

cases.name: policy.wrong-profile
cases.description: A different profile was required.

cases.name: policy.commit-not-allowed
cases.description: The OWASP commit is not in the verifier's allowed list.

cases.name: policy.downgrade
cases.description: DOWNGRADE DEFENCE: an attestation from when only AST03 existed cannot satisfy a verifier that requires all three controls, without parsing the assessment.

cases.name: policy.package-digest-mismatch
cases.description: The package on disk is not the one assessed.

cases.name: policy.fresh-enough
cases.description: Within the maximum age (verifier-supplied clock).

cases.name: policy.too-old
cases.description: Older than the maximum age.

cases.name: policy.retired-refused-by-default
cases.description: The reference default accepts KEY_ACTIVE only: a retired key is refused unless the policy opts in.

cases.name: policy.retired-opt-in.issuedAt-after-retiredAt
cases.description: Historical or offline verification explicitly opts into KEY_RETIRED. This is a policy choice, and says nothing about when the signature was made.

cases.name: policy.retired-opt-in.issuedAt-before-retiredAt
cases.description: The same opt-in with the dates the other way round: the same result.

cases.name: policy.revoked-never-accepted
cases.description: KEY_REVOKED is never accepted, even with valid signature mathematics and a policy that accepts everything acceptable.

cases.name: policy.invalid-lists-revoked
cases.description: A policy that LISTS KEY_REVOKED as acceptable is invalid, and fails closed.

cases.name: policy.invalid-empty
cases.description: An empty acceptedKeyStates is invalid.

cases.name: policy.invalid-unknown-state
cases.description: A state that is not an acceptable key state (there is no TRUSTED state) is invalid.

cases.name: policy.invalid-lists-unknown-key
cases.description: KEY_UNKNOWN cannot be listed as acceptable either.

cases.name: policy.no-key-set-fails-default
cases.description: Without a key set the key state is NOT_EVALUATED, which no policy accepts.

cases.name: policy.purpose-mismatch-refused
cases.description: KEY_PURPOSE_MISMATCH is refused by every policy.

cases.name: policy.rollback-detected-refused
cases.description: KEY_SET_ROLLBACK_DETECTED is refused by every policy.

cases.name: policy.unsupported-profile-cannot-satisfy
cases.description: Unknown profile fails closed for any security conclusion: integrity is VALID and the key is active, but the policy is NOT satisfied.

cases.name: policy.unsupported-profile-version-cannot-satisfy
cases.description: Unknown profile version fails closed for any security conclusion.

cases.name: policy.unsupported-schema-cannot-satisfy
cases.description: Unknown assessment schema fails closed for any security conclusion.
